minutes_text:
MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, AUGUST 4, 2021

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:
The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Special Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, August 4, 2021, in the City
Council Chambers, on the ninth floor, in City Hall. Following the
Pledge of Allegiance by Commissioner David Rice, the meeting was
called to order at 7:00 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:
Present: Chairman Larry Springs
  Commissioner Patricia Patrick
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams
Excused
Absence: Commissioner Aide Trejo

Staff:  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner
  Art Salazar, Planner
  Marissa Fewell, Planner
  Angel Leon-Martell, Assistant Planner
  Sean May, Planning Technician
  Christopher E. Jackson, Sr., ECD Director
  Jeff Lewis, Acting Assistant City Attorney
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary
  Via Community Phone Call Coverage:
  AT&T Conference Call Operator Rep.

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:
Ms. Wilcox, Planning Manager mentioned Commissioner Trejo
contacted staff to say she would not be attending this evening’s
Planning Commission Meeting. She also announced the promotion of
our newest Planning Technician, Sean May, previously an intern,
who replaces Angel Leon-Martell, who was promoted to Assistant
Planner.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
None, and the AT&T Operator verbally confirmed that there were no
participants on the line to speak.

(5) MINUTES APPROVAL:
Commissioner Rice made the motion to approve the Special Planning
Commission Meeting Minutes of March 11, 2020 and was seconded by
Commissioner Patrick.

MOTION:
The motion passed with the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, and Chairman Springs.
Abstained: Commissioner Shaw-Williams.

(6) PUBLIC HEARINGS:

6A: SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2021-003 (SP-2021-003) 339 EAST
PLYMOUTH.
A public hearing to consider an application by Gina Cabotaje,
representing HomeLight DayCare, for Special Use Permit No. 2021-
003 (SP-2021-003) to allow 1) a child day care facility and 2) a
reduced parking requirement through the use of alternative modes
of transportation in an existing three-story apartment building on
an  approximately  9,889  square-foot  (R-3)  Multiple-family
Residential zoned property at 339 East Plymouth.
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
August 4, 2021

Mr. Arturo Salazar, Planner, made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Rice asked staff several questions regarding – Zone
Variance, Loading and Unloading, Any Police Reports, and Street
utilization by the applicant.
   Mr. Salazar responded to the questions.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to come forward to address
the Planning Commission and speak about their project.

Ms. Gina Cabotaje, spoke to the Planning Commission via telephone
regarding her project and introduced Andrea Scarla and Ricardo
Rosales to answer questions from the Planning Commission.

Chairman Springs opened the floor for the Planning Commission to
address the applicant.

Commissioner Patrick asked the applicant questions regarding –
Parking of residential vehicles, fumes from the vehicles,
pedestrian safety regarding children of the daycare.
  - Ms. Scarla answered Commissioner Patrick’s questions.

Commissioner Rice asked staff regarding – If there were any Police
Reports for the area?
  - Mr. Salazar responded to the question.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked several questions of the
applicant regarding the total number of students, parking signs
for children’s safety, and why there is no 24 hour security service
during the week?
  - Ms. Scarla and Mr. Rosales answered Commissioner Shaw-
  Williams’ questions.

Chairman Springs asked several questions regarding if there are
families presently living at the site, also if there are any
children attending the school.
  - Mr. Rosales responded to Chairman Springs questions.

Chairman Springs opened the public hearing to the audience to
speak either for or against this project.

FOR / AGAINST:
Mr. John Reisick, Board Member and Chairman – For
Ms. Liz Poore, Board Member Midnight Mission & CEO – For
Mr. Mike Arnold, Resident of Midnight Mission – For
Dr. Chenoby – For
Ms. Monty, Inglewood Resident - For

Chairman Springs closed the public hearing and asked for any
final comments from the commissioners?

Commissioner Rice asked another question of staff – regarding
other Daycare centers in the area?
  - Mr. Salazar answered Commissioner Rice’s question.

Chairman Springs called for a motion.

  2
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
August 4, 2021
MOTION:
Commissioner Rice made the motion to affirm the categorical
exemption EA-CE-2020-076 and adopt the attached resolution
approving SP-2021-003, subject to 7 conditions, and the added two
conditions 1) One Year Review of project and 2) Adding of “Caution
Children in Area” Signs be posted and was seconded by Commissioner
Patrick, that Resolution No. 1900

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING A
  CERTAIN SPECIAL USE PERMIT TO ALLOW 1)A CHILD
  DAY CARE FACILITY AND 2)REDUCED PARKING
  REQUIREMENT THROUGH THE USE OF ALTERNATE MODES
  OF OTRANSPORTATION IN AN EXISTING THREE-STORY
  APARTMENT BUILDING ON AN APPROXIMATELY 9,889
  SQUARE-FOOT R-3 (MULTIPLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL)
  ZONED PROPERTY AT 339 EAST PLYMOUTH STREET

Be approved

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Shaw Williams and
  Chairman Springs.

Ms. Mindy Wilcox clarified that the one-year in review will be
dependent upon when the Business License is put into action and
she explained the appeal process.

6B: SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2021-007 (SP-2021-007), 3863 WEST
CENTURY BOULEVARD.
A public hearing to consider an application by J. D. Fox,
representing WDR, LLC, for AT&T, for Special Use Permit No. 2021-
007 (SP-2021-007) to allow the location of a roof-mounted wireless
telecommunication facility on the roof of an existing parking
garage on an approximately 3.6-acre, HPSP(Hollywood Park Specific
Plan) zoned property at 3863 West Century Boulevard.

Ms. Marissa Fewell, Planner, made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Patrick made a comment regarding the possibility of
traffic backup problems that the installation will cause on
Century Boulevard, and what is the City doing to prevent or
circumvent that?
   Ms. Fewell answered Commissioner Patrick’s question.

Commissioner Rice asked staff questions and made comments
regarding parking at the site.
   Ms. Fewell responded to Commissioner Rice’s question.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to come forward to address
the Planning Commission and speak about their project.
   Mr. J. D. Fox, came forward and spoke to the Planning
  Commission regarding his project on Plymouth Street.

Commissioner Rice asked the applicant to explain the process of
this particular antenna setup, what type of transmissions this
size of antenna will have on the surrounding community, and will
this antenna be shared by other telecom companies?
   Mr. Fox responded to Commissioner Rice’s question.

  3
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
August 4, 2021

Chairman Springs asked staff to explain the technical reasons and
purpose for this size antenna.
  - Ms. Fewell answered Chairman’s question.

Both Commissioner Rice and Chairman Springs asked the applicant
what will be the radiation output of this particular antenna?
  - Ms. Wilcox answered Commissioner and Chairman’s question.

Chairman Springs opened the public hearing to the audience to
speak either for or against this project.

FOR / AGAINST:
None

Chairman Springs closed the public hearing and asked for any
final questions or comments from the commissioners, seeing and
hearing none, Chairman Springs called for a motion.

Chairman Springs stated hearing no motion from the Planning
Commission, this item dies on the floor.

Assistant Attorney Lewis stated that it is within the Planning
Commission’s right to not make a motion regarding the item,
therefore it should be treated as a denial.

   Ms. Wilcox asked the Planning Commission to give a reason for
  the denial to be included in the Resolution.
   Mr. Jackson requested stated that this type of action has
  happened in the past and therefore the proceedings shall
  continue on as a denied action.

Chairman Springs asked Ms. Wilcox to explain the appeals process.

Further discussion was had with the Assistant City Attorney and
the planning commission, regarding if this item can be continued
to the next Planning Commission meeting of September 2021, to allow
the applicant to return before the planning commission with expert
assistance to explain the purpose and use along with any technical
questions the planning commissioners may have.

Chairman Springs asked for a motion from the Planning Commission

MOTION:

Commissioner Rice made the motion to Continue this item until the
September 1, 2021 Planning Commission Meeting, and it was seconded
by Commissioner Shaw-Williams

Chairman Springs asked if there are any questions, there were none, he
called for the vote.

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Shaw-Williams and Chairman
  Springs.

Mr. Jackson made mention for the record that since the Planning
Commission has decided to continue this item, there is no appealing
this decision.

  4
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
August 4, 2021

6C: SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2021-008 (SP-2021-008), 4940 WEST
CENTURY BOULEVARD.
A public hearing to consider an application by Michael Acevedo,
representing 405 Century Plaza LLC, for Special Use Permit No.
2021-008 (SP-2021-008) to allow a barbershop within 300 feet of a
similar use on an approximately 1.59-acre, C-2A (Airport
Commercial) zoned property at 4940 West Century Boulevard.

Mr. Angel Leon-Martell,  Assistant  Planner  made  the  staff
presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Patrick made a statement and asked about security
cameras at the site.
  - Mr. Leon-Martell answered Commissioner Patrick’s question.

Chairman Springs asked staff multiple questions regarding his
concerns about security cameras and the fact that it is a very
busy business along with questions about the other nail salon near
the applicant’s site.
  - Mr. Leon-Martell answered Chairman Springs’ question.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to addressed the Planning
Commission and speak about his project.
  - Mr. Acevedo attempted to talk with the Planning Commission,
  but due to technical difficulties, the call was ended.
  - Mr. Leon-Martell represented the applicant and answered the
  Commissioners questions.

Commissioner Patrick asked staff to confirm that the applicant
will be supplying security cameras that will cover the entire
complex.
  - Mr. Leon-Martell answered Commissioner Patrick’s question.

Commissioner Rice asked staff if the applicant’s business will
support the community in any way.
  - Mr. Leon-Martell answered Commissioner Rice’s question.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked staff if the applicant mentioned
that there is parking in the rear of the building?
  - Mr.  Leon-Martell  answered  Commissioner  Shaw-Williams’
  question.

Chairman Springs opened the public hearing to the audience to speak
either for or against this project.

FOR / AGAINST:
None – (Confirmed by the AT&T Operator).

Chairman Springs closed the public hearing and asked for any final
questions or comments from the commissioners, seeing and hearing
none, Chairman Springs called for a motion.

  5
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
August 4, 2021
MOTION:
Commissioner Shaw-Williams made the motion to affirm the
categorical exemption EA-CE-2021-051, and adopt the attached
resolution approving SP-2021-008 subject to the 13 conditions and
was seconded by Commissioner Patrick, that Resolution No. 1902

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING A
  CERTAIN SPECIAL USE PERMIT TO MICHAEL ACEVEDO
  REPRESENTING 405 CENTURY PLAZA, LLC., TO ALLOW
  A BARBERSHOP, WITHIN 300 FEET OF A SIMILAR USE
  ON AN APPROXIMATELY 1.59 ACRE, C-2A (AIRPORT
  COMMERCIAL) ZONED PROPERTY AT 4940 WEST
  CENTURY BOULEVARD

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Shaw-Williams and Chairman
  Springs.

Ms. Wilcox explained there is no appeals process.

6D. ZONING CODE AMENDMENT NO. 2021-001 (ZCA-20210-001) CHAPTER 12
IMC: A public hearing to consider Zoning Code Amendment 2021-001
(ZCA-2021-001) to Chapter 12 of the Inglewood Municipal Code to
modify regulations for Smoke Shops, citywide.

Mr. Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner, made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Patrick made a statement to staff with regards to
smoke shops being too close to schools.

Commissioner Rice had no comments or questions at this time.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams stated no questions or comments at this
time.

Chairman Springs stated he had no comments or questions.

Chairman Springs opened the public hearing and opened up the phone
line to allow the public to speak for or against this item.

FOR / AGAINST:

None (Confirmed by the AT&T Operator)

Chairman Springs closed the public hearing.

Chairman Springs asked for closing questions or comments from the
Commissioners.

Commissioner Patrick had several statements for staff:
 For clarification on this Zoning Code Amendment, the smoke shops
  will be required to have a distance of one–mile separation is
  this correct? Also with the size of Inglewood, it would not be
  too hard for all of these existing smoke shops to already be
  within one-mile separation of other retail shops, not to mention
  one another and still have space for more.
   Mr. McCrumby stated yes, that is correct. Based on the map
  created by staff, there is the possibility to add
  approximately three more Smoke Shops.

  6
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
August 4, 2021

  Remember the problems that come with the various Smoke Shops,
  there was the one on 110th and Crenshaw, and the example of the
  old shop on Crenshaw and Manchester Boulevard, the fact that
  IPD had to frequent that location on a weekly basis.

Commissioner Rice stated that he is glad that the planning division
is staying ahead of the game in insuring that the City is not fully
saturated with these pop-up smoke shops.

Chairman Springs asked for a motion from the Planning Commission.

MOTION:
The motion was made by Commissioner Rice to affirm categorical
exemption EA-CE-2021-020, and adopt a resolution recommending City
Council adoption of Zoning Code Amendment 2021-001 (ZCA-2021-001)
and was seconded by Commissioner Patrick that Resolution No. 1903;

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING AND
  RECOMMENDING TO THE CITY COUNCIL FOR APPROVAL
  ZONING CODE AMENDMENT 2021-001 (ZCA-2021-001)
  TO ESTABLISH REGULATIONS FOR SMOKE SHOPS
  CITYWIDE.

Be approved.

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Shaw-Williams and Chairman
  Springs

There are no appeal options and this will be sent directly to
the City Council for their consideration, per Ms. Wilcox.

(7) NON-PUBLIC HEARING:

7A: DESIGN REVIEW 2021-005 (DR-2021-005).
A non-public hearing to consider an application by Sandy Sigal,
representing NewMark Merrill Companies, for Design Review No.
2021-005 (DR-2021-005) to allow a 936 square-foot mural on the
exterior of a one-story commercial building that is part of an
existing shopping center on an approximately 17-acre, C-2(General
Commercial) zoned property at 2876 West Imperial Highway.

Mr. Arturo Salazar, Planner made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Patrick asked staff:
 On behalf of the applicant staff is asking this body to approve
  what is already up without a permit, and what was approved is
  not at the site?
  - Mr. Salazar stated that is correct.

Commissioner Rice questioned staff:
 Regarding the actual size of the art and the size of the
  building, along with what is presently on the building.

  7
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
August 4, 2021
Commissioner Shaw-Williams made a comment to staff:
 Regarding what was actually approved and what eventually was
  presented and that all expectations were not realized.

Chairman Springs stated that he also agrees with Commissioner Shaw-
Williams and asked for the applicant to address the Planning
Commission at this time.

Mr. Tim Murphy speaking on behalf of NewMark Merrill Companies.

Commissioner Rice made several statements to the applicant with
regards to NewMark Merrill doing what they wanted to do, instead
of what was approved by this body to do.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams questioned Mr. Murphy regarding NewMark
Merrill utilizing another artist to replicate what was approved?
  - Mr. Murphy stated that the approved artwork was patented and
  therefore NewMark Merrill opted to go with another artist
  utilizing the same message.

Chairman Springs stated his dislike and disdain for the non-
consideration of the company towards the community, the planning
commission and the city council in showing such disrespect to this
community.

Assistant City Attorney Lewis stated to the Planning Commission
with regards to the decision of the Commission and if it is towards
Denial of the Mural, that in making the motion these facts should
be entered into the motion and record, the aesthetics of the
design, the size in proportion to the building, color scheme is
not what was approved, neither was the final design.

Ms. Wilcox also stated for the Planning Commission that technically
this is a new application.

Commissioner Patrick stated that at this point she is confused as
to what is being voted on this evening, is it for the Planning
Commission to approve what is presently up on the wall, or to have
it removed from the wall and place what was initially approved
onto the wall or start over with something new.

Mr. Christopher Jackson, Sr., stated to the planning commission
that at present, technically what is up on the wall is not
approved, and the city’s code enforcement has been holding back on
citing NewMark Merrill, because if they do, the applicant will
have to take down what is presently up and put the wall back to
its original state – blank. He also stated that the company has
done very well by what has taken place so far in the area with
regards to bringing new vitalization, revamping and life to the
plaza, so this is something to keep in consideration with regards
to your denial.

Chairman Springs closed the floor and called for the motion.

  8
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
August 4, 2021
MOTION:
Commissioner Rice made the motion to Deny the categorical
exemption EA-CE-2021-074, and adopt a resolution recommending
denial to the City Council of DR-2021-005 for these various
reasons, aesthetic issues, the design, and proportion to the wall
it is not scaled appropriately, the location, the subject of the
art and especially the color scheme and was seconded by
Commissioner Shaw-Williams, that Resolution No. 1904

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALFORNIA, DENYING AN
  APPLICATION BY SANDY SIGAL, REPRESENTING
  NEWMARK MERRILL COMPANIES, FOR DESIGN REVIEW
  (DR-2021-008) TO ALLOW A  936 SQUARE-FOOT
  MURAL ON THE EXTERIOR OF AN EXISTING SHOPPING
  ENTER ON AN APPROXIMATELY 17 ACRE, C-2
  (GENERAL COMMERCIAL) PROPERTY LOCATED AT 2876
  WEST IMPERIAL HIGHWAY.

Be approved.

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Shaw-Williams and Chairman
  Springs.

Ms. Wilcox explained the appeal process.

Chairman Springs stated that Commissioner Patrick reminded him
that the plaza area is still not complete and this has been for
several years now. There was a promise of an outdoor
entertainment area, a stage area where there would be music all
year round as well as other outdoor entertainment for the
community and it has yet to take place.

Mr. Jackson asked Ms. Wilcox if she had any information at
present time or did she want to wait and come back to the
Planning Commission at a later date.

Ms. Wilcox stated that there still is activity and work being
done and modifications to the rear area of the plaza and the
completion is still yet to come, but staff will need to return
to the planning commission at a later date with more
information.

Mr. Jackson stated that there is still an outstanding bond with
regards to this project. There are many strict reasons as to
meeting the state regulations and federal standards that come
into play when doing such a large process. Staff will come back
to the planning commission after some more research.

(8)  PUBLIC COMMENTS:
1.  Mr. Pablo Arnold – Inglewood Resident of District-4
  He ask if district four will be widening the streets anytime
  soon? It is so difficult at present, with cars on both
  sides of the street, in this district, it is very difficult
  to get through safely, and possibly there can be one day of
  the week where there is parking only on one-side of the
  street and also maybe have the street parking lined so that
  people cannot block two spaces, while holding spots for
  other vehicles.

Ms. Wilcox stated that he should contact both Parking and also
the Traffic Commission in regards to this.

  9
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
August 4, 2021
Chairman Springs closed the hearings to the public and asked for
the Planning Commission Initiatives.

(9) COMMISSION INITIATIVES:
Commissioner Patrick –
 Thank you to the community for listening and watching and stay
  safe.

Commissioner Rice -
 Good evening everyone and stay safe.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams –
 Everyone stay safe see you next month.

(10) ADJOURNMENT:
Chairman Springs wished everyone a good evening and adjourned
tonight’s meeting.
